text: Hint 1: To find the value of $\hat{\theta}$ that minimizes the Mean Squared Error (MSE), consider the formula for MSE: $\text{MSE} $$=$$ \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}**{n} (y_i - \hat{y}_i)**2$. Substitute $\hat{y}_i $$=$$ $$\theta$$ \ln(x_i**2)$ into this formula.\n\nHint 2: Remember that the MSE is a convex function with respect to $\theta$. To find the minimum, take the derivative of the MSE with respect to $\theta$, set it to zero, and solve for $\theta$. This will give you the expression for $\hat{\theta}$ in terms of $x_i$, $y_i$, and $n$.
